AUTHOR: Siddiqui
TITLE: Automatic fish species classification in underwater videos: Exploiting pre-trained deep neural network models to compensate for limited labelled data
REGION: Western Australia, Cape Naturaliste to Houtman Abrolhos Islands (kelp, seagrass, sand, coral reef habitats, 5-50 m depth)
SPECIES: 16 focal species incl. Pentapodus porosus, P. emeryii, Choerodon rubescens, C. cyanodus, Abudefduf bengalensis, Plectropomus leopardus, Lethrinus nebulosus, L. atkinsoni, Lethrinus sp., Carangoides fulvoguttatus, Lutjanus carponotatus, Scarus ghobban, Scombridae spp., Thalassoma lunare, Coris auricularis, Pagrus auratus + 'other' class
DATA: Own stereo-BRUV footage (2011-2013), 10-s clips per species, 2,209 cropped 224x224 still images (Table 1); secondary experiment on LifeCLEF 2015 (Fish4Knowledge) images
V_EV: Methods: 'Videos were collected from kelp, seagrass, sand and coral reef habitats between 5 and 50 m of water depth'; Fig. 1 caption: 'complexity and challenges in the data in the form of murkiness, blurriness'
D_EV: Methods: 'From the video clips, still images were extracted, re-sized and cropped' ; Table 1 gives train/val/test counts only (allocation unit never stated)
R_EV: Discussion: 'we only trained the SVM (for classification) on features extracted by the same pre-trained ResNet-152b with cross-layer pooling on the images of LifeClef'15'
C_EV: Methods: 'A one-vs.-all linear SVM was trained on the cross-pooled features for classification of the fish species.'
E_EV: Results: 'A classification accuracy of 94.3% was achieved when classifying only the 16 fish species' — accuracy, precision, recall and confusion matrix only
ARCH: Pre-trained AlexNet / VGGNet / ResNet-152 as frozen feature extractors with cross-layer pooling (+PCA), one-vs-all linear SVM (LibSVM, MatConvNet)
METR: Accuracy 94.3% (16 species), 89.0% incl. 'other' class; per-species precision/recall (Fig. 7); 96.73% on LifeCLEF'15
NOTE: V2/V3/V4 interpreted as depth / illumination / camera-to-subject range respectively (schema does not label them); depth range 5-50 m reported (V2 = Y). Turbidity/murkiness mentioned qualitatively only. The authors attribute higher LifeCLEF'15 accuracy to 'relatively clear images' but this is a cross-dataset remark, not stratified evaluation (V6 = N; verifier may consider P). Split unit not stated: roughly 50-120 10-s clips per species yielding ~100 images per species, so images may be near one-per-clip, but this is not stated (D1 = NR). LifeCLEF'15 experiment retrains the SVM on that dataset (5% per class), so it is a second in-domain experiment, not external validation (R1 = N). Dataset collected during MaxN analysis but AI output is not connected to MaxN or any ecological variable.
